description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; ASCII-probed.

`can()` on a FORWARD-DECLARED sub (`sub NAME;`, declared and never defined)
returns a CODE ref in perl and UNDEF in PCL:

    package Alice;
    sub sing;                 # forward declaration, never defined
    sub drink { "drinking" }
    package main;
    my $a = bless {}, 'Alice';
    $a->can("drink")   perl CODE   PCL CODE
    $a->can("sing")    perl CODE   PCL undef        <-- the divergence
    calling it         perl dies   PCL dies         (both: undefined subroutine)

perl's `can` hands back the GV's CV, which exists for a declared-but-undefined
sub; calling it is what dies.  So `can` is a question about DECLARATION, not
about definedness.

WHERE, AND WHY IT IS DELIBERATE TODAY: `p-can` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp skips a
sub whose `*p-declared-subs*` entry is `:stub`, with the comment "A
forward-declaration STUB is fboundp but not a real method (Perl wouldn't have
compiled it yet) -- ignore it, matching p-stash.  See
docs/declaration-ordering-fix-plan.md".  So the skip exists because PCL's
phase model binds a sub's symbol EARLIER than perl compiles the sub, and
`can` must not answer yes for something perl has not seen.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN s473t5f: removing the skip needs the measurement the
comment implies -- WHICH subs get the `:stub` mark.  If it is only explicit
`sub NAME;` forward declarations, removing the skip is right and free.  If PCL
also marks a not-yet-compiled later definition, removing it turns `can` into a
yes for subs perl would say no to at that point in the file, and `can` is the
single most common feature probe in CPAN code.  MEASURE FIRST: instrument
`*p-declared-subs*` over the corpus and list the shapes that reach `:stub`.

WHAT IT COSTS: `t/uni/universal.t` row 16 (`ok $ref = $a->can(...)`, where the
file forward-declares that sub).  One row here; the shape is common enough in
real modules (a forward declaration for a prototype) that the divergence is
worth closing.
subject: can() on a FORWARD-DECLARED sub returns a CODE ref in perl and undef in PCL -- p-can skips :stub deliberately; measure which shapes get that mark before removing the skip
